records.claim: One study looked at whether past use of erythromycin affected sperm quality. The study suggested that erythromycin use might be linked to lower sperm count (number of sperm) and lower sperm movement (motility). However, the study did not look at the dose, timing, or reason the antibiotic was used. Because of this, the results may not show the true effect of erythromycin on the sperm. Studies have not been done to see if erythromycin could increase the chance of birth defects. In general, exposures that men have are less likely to increase the risks to a pregnancy. For more information, please see the MotherToBaby fact sheet Paternal Exposures at https://mothertobaby.org/fact-sheets/paternal-exposures-pregnancy/.
records.source_section: If a man takes erythromycin, could it affect fertility or increase the chance of birth defects?
